topic_summary: Analysis of the moral-status boundary debate between pro-life and pro-choice positions, centered on when personhood begins. The personhood-boundary kernel is read at conception, viability, or birth, with each reading emitting a constraint with a fundamentally different victim set and rights structure.

key_entities: National Right to Life Committee (NRLC) - leading pro-life advocacy organization
Students for Life of America - largest pro-life youth organization
Planned Parenthood - largest reproductive health services provider including abortion
Catholic Church - religious authority grounding conception reading
U.S. Supreme Court - constitutional adjudicator pre-Dobbs
Pregnant woman - rights-holder in autonomy framework
key_tensions: Conception vs viability vs birth as personhood threshold (kernel contest)
Fetal rights vs maternal bodily autonomy (competing rights frameworks)
Federal constitutional framework vs state-by-state determination (post-Dobbs)
Incremental strategy vs sweeping bans (pro-life internal)
Personhood recognition vs abortion access (slippery slope)
Religious authority vs secular autonomy grounding

omegas.description: Historical 'quickening' standard (fetal movement ~16-20 weeks) was common law personhood threshold pre-19th century. Why did this reading collapse? Technological visibility (ultrasound) or religious mobilization?

Brain death defines end-of-life personhood in medical ethics. Why is neurological development (cortical activity ~24-28 weeks) not the dominant beginning-of-life threshold? Asymmetry suggests non-biological grounding.

All three readings are debated primarily by institutions with male leadership (Catholic hierarchy, Supreme Court pre-RBG, state legislatures). Does the kernel contest itself extract authority from pregnant women to male-dominated adjudicators?

Conception reading claims embryo = person, yet IVF clinics routinely dispose of unused embryos without pro-life mobilization at scale. Is this a Piton (selective enforcement) revealing the reading's true extractiveness target (abortion access, not embryo protection)?
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) + Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Conception reading holds embryo = person with rights from fertilization; birth reading holds fetus = non-person until birth. No coherent framework can simultaneously hold both 'embryo has right to life' and 'fetus has no rights until birth' as foundational axioms.

Conception reading grounds personhood in biological origin (fertilization); viability reading grounds personhood in technological threshold (survivability outside womb). No coherent framework can hold both 'personhood is intrinsic to human organism from conception' and 'personhood is contingent on external technological capacity' as foundational axioms.
